Name: Define
Goal: Turn the request into a precise, testable statement of done.
Key Activities: Restate the task in one sentence; write expected vs actual (bug) or acceptance criteria (feature); note constraints and what is out of scope; ask when intent is ambiguous.
Quality Gate: A check you can run that fails today and must pass when done: a failing test, a repro command, a benchmark baseline or written acceptance criteria.
Evidence: The repro command and its output, the failing test name, or the acceptance criteria list.
Pitfalls: Starting to code before knowing what done looks like; accepting a vague report; solving a different problem than the one asked.

Name: Decompose
Goal: Map the change: where it lives and what it touches.
Key Activities: Find entry points and trace the call path; list files, modules and layers involved; note data and schema touched; check callers of anything you will change; read recent history of the area (git log).
Quality Gate: A change map: files and functions to read or modify, and who calls them.
Evidence: List of paths with one line each on their role; the call path from input to output.
Pitfalls: Guessing structure instead of reading code; missing callers in other packages; ignoring config, migrations and tests as part of the change.

Name: Prioritize
Goal: Choose the smallest safe slice and the order of work.
Key Activities: Rank hypotheses or slices by value and risk; do risky unknowns early with a spike; push nice-to-haves out; cap active branches of work at three.
Quality Gate: An ordered list where the first item is small enough to finish and verify on its own.
Evidence: The ordered list with the first slice marked.
Pitfalls: Starting with the most interesting part instead of the riskiest; trying to do everything in one pass.

Name: Plan
Goal: Decide how each slice is built, tested and undone.
Key Activities: Write the task list; for each task name the test that proves it; decide feature flag, migration and rollback; note docs and config to update.
Quality Gate: Every task has a test or check attached and a way back if it goes wrong.
Evidence: Task checklist with the test per task and the rollback note.
Pitfalls: Plans without tests; no rollback for data or API changes; plans so detailed they replace thinking with paperwork.

Name: Execute
Goal: Make the change in small, verified steps.
Key Activities: Work one task or hypothesis at a time; run the relevant tests after each step; keep a log of what you tried and observed; commit at each green step.
Quality Gate: Each step ends green, and the log explains every change made.
Evidence: The hypothesis or progress log and the sequence of green commits.
Pitfalls: Several speculative edits at once; leaving debug code behind; silencing errors to make tests pass.

Name: Verify
Goal: Prove the result against the definition from Step 1.
Key Activities: Re-run the Step 1 check; run the full test suite, linter, type checker and build; review the diff against the review checklist; check edge and error paths; compare numbers for performance work.
Quality Gate: The Step 1 check now passes and the project's own checks are green. Every claim is backed by output you actually ran.
Evidence: Commands run with their results; before/after numbers where relevant.
Pitfalls: Declaring success without running checks; testing only the happy path; trusting a passing test that never failed.

Name: Communicate
Goal: Hand the change over so others can trust and review it.
Key Activities: Write the artifact for the task (PR description, ADR, postmortem, review report); lead with the outcome; include evidence, risks, rollback and follow-ups.
Quality Gate: A reviewer can understand what changed, why it is safe and how it was verified without asking.
Evidence: The PR description or other artifact.
Pitfalls: Narrating the process instead of the outcome; hiding known risks; no test evidence.
